title: Swan Lake by World Ballet Company
description: The World’s MOST Iconic Ballet – With a LIVE Orchestra!
big_desc: The World’s MOST Iconic Ballet – With a LIVE Orchestra! The legendary tale of Swan Lake takes flight in a breathtaking production from World Ballet Company, as fate and magic entwine in a timeless battle between good and evil. Performing with a Live Orchestra, and featuring a cast of 50 international dancers, over 150 radiant hand-sewn costumes, and stunning hand-crafted sets, this spellbinding ballet captures every heart-pounding moment – from the Dance of the Little Swans to the Black Swan’s 32 fouettés, and every pirouette in between. With Tchaikovsky’s unforgettable score soaring through the air and played LIVE, immerse yourself in this mesmerizing journey where dreams, heartbreak, and hope unfold right before your eyes. Duration: 2 hours 30 minutes (including 20-minute intermission) Audience: For ages 5 & over WBC Website: https://worldballetcompany.com/federalway2 World Ballet Company – Ballet Everywhere, Ballet For All. *About the Company: Based in Los Angeles, and led by Sasha Gorskaya and Gulya Hartwick, World Ballet Company presents the most beloved and iconic ballets of our time in cities nationwide. Driven by the belief that ballet is for everyone, performances appeal to newcomers and seasoned ballet goers alike. The company attracts many international artists and comprises renowned professional dancers representing over ten countries. To date, World Ballet Company has traveled to more than 300 cities, reaching an audience of more than 500,000 fans. Make it a group experience! Special pricing is available for groups of 10 or more: worldballetcompany.com/group-tickets.

title: A VERY MERRY CHRISTMAS SHOW
description: From the producers of the hit ’60s Flashback Show comes A Very Merry Christmas Show — a spectacular, all-new holiday celebration filled with music, memories and Christmas magic!
big_desc: From the producers of the hit ’60s Flashback Show comes A Very Merry Christmas Show — a spectacular, all-new holiday celebration filled with music, memories and Christmas magic! Featuring more than 20 of the Northwest’s favorite vocalists and an incredible cast of dancers, A Very Merry Christmas Show takes audiences on an unforgettable journey through Christmas past to present — from the beloved songs and traditions of the 1940s and ’50s, through the unforgettable Christmas television specials of the ’60s and ’70s, and all the way to the holiday favorites we love today. Expect soaring vocals, show-stopping dance numbers, dazzling costumes, heartwarming nostalgia and treasured memories of Christmases gone by — all brought to life in the same high-energy, nostalgic style audiences loved in ’60s Flashback. After sold-out performances in Seattle, this much-loved holiday production is coming south for one special night at the Federal Way Performing Arts & Events Center. And the magic doesn’t end when the curtain comes down! Santa Claus will be waiting in the lobby after the show to meet the kids, making this a Christmas memory the whole family can share. This year, A Very Merry Christmas Show is also proud to partner with local charity PB&J for the Homeless. Guests are invited to join in the spirit of giving by bringing a jar of peanut butter or jelly to donate in the lobby on the night of the performance. Kick-start your Christmas spirit with an unforgettable night of music, dancing, laughter, nostalgia and holiday magic for the whole family. And be ready for a magical finale you won’t soon forget.

title: Arts 4 Youth: STOMP
description: STOMP is explosive, provocative, sophisticated, utterly unique and appeals to audiences of all ages. The international percussion sensation has garnered an armful of awards and rave reviews, and has appeared on numerous national television shows. The eight-member troupe uses everything but conventional percussion instruments – matchboxes, wooden poles, brooms, garbage cans, Zippo lighters, hubcaps – to fill the stage with magnificent rhythms. The return of the percussive hit also brings some new surprises, with some sections of the show now updated and restructured and the addition of two new full-scale routines, utilizing props like tractor tire inner tubes and paint cans. As USA Today says, “STOMP finds beautiful noises in the strangest places.” STOMP. See what all the noise is about.

venue_name: Federal Way Performing Arts and Event Center
address: 31510 Pete von Reichbauer Way S Federal Way, WA 98003
title: K-TROT SPECIAL CONCERT KIM SOO CHAN & MARIA
description: Two captivating voices. The heart of Korean music. One unforgettable evening.
big_desc: Two captivating voices. The heart of Korean music. One unforgettable evening. Experience the energy, emotion, and charm of Korean Trot with Kim Soo Chan & Maria, live at the Federal Way Performing Arts and Event Center on February 13, 2027, at 7 PM Known for its expressive vocals, memorable melodies, and heartfelt storytelling, trot holds a cherished place in Korean popular music. Its songs bring generations together through stories of love, longing, resilience, and joy. This special concert introduces audiences to that enduring tradition through two artists who bring their own distinctive voices to the stage. Kim Soo Chan is one of Korea’s most charismatic young trot entertainers, recognized for his appearances on Mr. Trot, Hidden Singer 2, and Active King of Singers 2. Combining powerful vocals with energetic choreography, playful humor, and impressions of legendary Korean singers, he brings a vibrant spirit to every performance. His engaging stage presence gives classic trot a fresh appeal while honoring the music that audiences have loved for decades. Maria, an American-born singer who established her career in Korea, brings a remarkable story of cultural connection. Through appearances on Miss Trot 2 and Active King of Singers, she won audiences over with her expressive voice, heartfelt delivery, and deep appreciation for Korean music. Comfortable communicating in both Korean and English, she offers a warm welcome to longtime trot fans and those discovering the genre for the first time. Together, Kim Soo Chan and Maria celebrate the growing international appeal of Korean trot—music rooted in tradition and brought to life with personality, passion, and contemporary energy. For Korean-American audiences, the evening offers a connection to familiar sounds and cherished memories. For new listeners, it opens the door to a rich and spirited musical world. Join us for an evening of soaring vocals, heartfelt melodies, and joyful entertainment as Kim Soo Chan & Maria bring Korean Trot to Federal Way We open our doors to accommodate all different types of entertainment, genres, and events to serve all of the people in our community and beyond. venue_name: Federal Way Performing Arts and Event Center
title: Auburn Symphony Orchestra: The Music of Studio Ghibli
description: This concert will not have Joe Hisaishi in attendance nor show any of the films.
big_desc: This concert will not have Joe Hisaishi in attendance nor show any of the films. A girl takes flight on a broomstick. A forest spirit waits beneath the trees. A young girl wanders into a bathhouse for gods. A castle lumbers across the hills on impossible legs. For generations of fans, Studio Ghibli has created animated films that feel both fantastical and deeply human. Founded in Japan and closely associated with filmmaker Hayao Miyazaki, the studio has become one of the most beloved names in animation, with stories known for wonder, adventure, environmental beauty, and characters who find courage in unfamiliar worlds. At the heart of many of those films is the music of Joe Hisaishi. His scores do more than accompany the action. They give these worlds their breath, motion, and emotional pull. Like John Williams’ long partnership with Steven Spielberg, Hisaishi’s music has helped shape the identity of the films themselves. Led by Music Director Wesley Schulz, Auburn Symphony celebrates the music of Kiki’s Delivery Service, My Neighbor Totoro, Spirited Away, and Howl’s Moving Castle in a concert filled with soaring melodies, playful characters, sweeping orchestral color, and moments of quiet beauty. Fans will recognize the themes they love. New listeners will hear why this music has reached far beyond the screen. The Music of Studio Ghibli is a concert for families, anime fans, film lovers, and anyone ready for an evening of adventure, nostalgia, and imagination.

venue_name: Federal Way Performing Arts and Event Center
title: Auburn Symphony Orchestra: Symphonic Stories
description: Some forces are invisible, but you feel their pull.
big_desc: Some forces are invisible, but you feel their pull. Symphonic Stories brings together three works about distance, memory, imagination, and the stories that hold us together. A voice reaches across grief. A soloist moves through shifting celestial worlds. A woman tells story after story, surviving one night at a time. Jennifer Higdon’s blue cathedral begins the journey in a place of remembrance. Written after the death of her brother, Andrew Blue Higdon, the piece imagines a vast sacred space filled with light, crystal, and upward motion. The flute, Higdon’s instrument, and the clarinet, her brother’s instrument, move through the music like two voices reaching toward one another. It is a work of loss, but also of release: a quiet ascent through memory toward something larger. From there, Auburn Symphony looks outward with the Co-Commission of Gravity at a Distance, a new saxophone concerto by Viet Cuong written for Timothy McAllister. The concerto takes inspiration from celestial bodies and the unseen forces that bind them across immense distances. The solo saxophone moves through orchestral worlds that feel luminous, floating, dense, and immense, tracing a path between isolation and attraction, stillness and motion. Then comes one of music’s great storytellers. Rimsky-Korsakov’s Scheherazade draws from One Thousand and One Nights, where Scheherazade survives a violent ruler not through force, but through intelligence, wit, and imagination. Each night, she tells a story compelling enough to earn another dawn. In the orchestra, her voice returns through the solo violin: persuasive, resilient, and unbroken. With blue cathedral, Gravity at a Distance, and Scheherazade, Symphonic Stories becomes a concert about what connects us across silence, space, and danger. These are stories of remembrance, invention, and survival, told in the language of the orchestra.

title: PAEC PRESENTS: The Wellermen
description: Follow the guiding star to a night of unforgettable harmony, storytelling, and adventure.
big_desc: Follow the guiding star to a night of unforgettable harmony, storytelling, and adventure. Complete your journey through 26–27 PAEC Presents Season: A Season That Shines with The Wellermen , the internationally acclaimed folk group whose soaring harmonies and captivating performances have inspired audiences around the world. The Wellermen first captured global attention in 2021 when their viral sea shanty performances ignited the worldwide “”Wellerman”” phenomenon. Since then, they have evolved into one of contemporary folk music’s most exciting live acts, blending East Coast American folk traditions with British musicianship and theatrical performance to create a sound that is both timeless and refreshingly modern. Known for their signature five-part harmonies and rare dual-bass vocal foundation, The Wellermen deliver rich, immersive performances filled with heartfelt storytelling, infectious energy, and songs that invite audiences to sing along. Their original music, including their acclaimed EP 1778 and their newest studio recordings, honors the spirit of traditional folk while charting an exciting new course for the genre. With successful international tours and a growing global following, The Wellermen continue to prove that their remarkable journey extends far beyond the sea shanties that first introduced them to millions. Their live performances celebrate community, connection, and the enduring power of music to bring people together. As the final constellation in 26–27 PAEC Presents Season: A Season That Shines , The Wellermen invite you to gather for an unforgettable evening of music, laughter, and shared stories. Raise your voice, join the chorus, and experience the joy of live folk music that will leave your spirits lifted long after the final note has faded. venue_name: Federal Way Performing Arts and Event Center
title: Auburn Symphony Orchestra: Rhythm & Revelry
description: A season finale is a celebration.
big_desc: A season finale is a celebration. Rhythm & Revelry begins with sacred joy in Omar Thomas’ Come Sunday, a tribute to the Hammond organ’s central place in Black worship. The first movement, “Testimony,” prepares the spirit with a sound world shaped by Bach, blues, jazz, and R&B. The second, “Shout!,” bursts into the ecstatic moment when celebration takes over. Thomas writes with love, energy, and purpose, honoring Black culture through music that sings, moves, and lifts the room. From there, the spotlight turns to violinist Nathan Amaral in Tchaikovsky’s Violin Concerto. Born in Rio de Janeiro, Amaral began violin through a social project in Mangueira and has since become one of the most compelling young violinists on the international stage. He won First Prize at the 2024 Sphinx Competition and the Grand Prize of the 2024 CAG-YCAT Competitions, and Yo-Yo Ma has praised his rare ability to move beyond technique into the heart of musical expression. Tchaikovsky’s concerto gives him a perfect canvas: soaring melodies, dazzling passagework, and emotional sweep from first note to last. Then Auburn Symphony takes center stage. Ravel’s Boléro begins with a single rhythm and one unforgettable theme, repeating again and again as the music grows from a whisper to a blaze. Each section of the orchestra gets its moment to shine, turning one simple idea into a thrilling display of color and control. Strauss’ Der Rosenkavalier Suite brings the afternoon to a lavish close. Drawn from his beloved opera, the suite mixes romantic sweep with elegant waltzes and the glittering richness of Vienna imagined through Strauss’ 20th-century orchestral voice. From worship to virtuosity to full-orchestra spectacle, Rhythm & Revelry sends the season out with brilliance, abundance, and joy.

The international percussion sensation has garnered an armful of awards and rave reviews, and has appeared on numerous national television shows. The eight-member troupe uses everything but conventional percussion instruments – matchboxes, wooden poles, brooms, garbage cans, Zippo lighters, hubcaps – to fill the stage with magnificent rhythms. The return of the percussive hit also brings some new surprises, with some sections of the show now updated and restructured and the addition of two new full-scale routines, utilizing props like tractor tire inner tubes and paint cans.
